_spec: EVERYTHING NUMERIC OR CHROMATIC IN THE KIT, AS DATA. The engine reads this file; no draw function hardcodes a colour or a length. Prose describing a colour is not a colour, so there is none here. Authored by eye and by hand — nothing in this file is computed from anything else in it, which is the whole point of §5: a shade is a picked colour, not a function of its lit.
supersedes: engine/plates.js ROLES + the per-author colour literals of delta-15. The hand-drawn kit's palette was one light-paper set with everything else multiplied down from it.

proportion._unit: HU — one head height, crown to chin. Every length here is in HU, so the figure has ONE size number and everything else is a ratio. A pose cannot disagree with another pose about how long an arm is.
proportion._widthsMoved: SEVEN WIDTHS MOVED at rebuild-02, none of them vertical, so the closure above is untouched and totalHeight is still 7.00. shoulderWidth 2.05 -> 1.80: at 2.05 the shoulder line is 2.6 head widths and the torso reads as a slab with a head on it, which is a proportion complaint of exactly the kind 7.0 HU exists to answer — it was simply the horizontal one, and nobody had measured it. glassesWidth 0.72 -> 0.62, lens height 0.24 -> 0.20, radius 0.07 -> 0.06: at 0.72 the frames span 92% of the head width and the face is a pair of frames. eyeDash 0.12 -> 0.10 and its weight 0.045 -> 0.038: two heavy bars in big lenses read vacant rather than deadpan. handLength 0.52 -> 0.46, handWidth 0.34 -> 0.30: the mitten was reading as a mitt.
proportion._closes: shoulderFromCrown 1.32 + torsoLength 2.45 = hipFromCrown 3.77; + legUpperLength 1.60 + legLowerLength 1.63 = 7.00 = totalHeight. The table is arithmetically closed on purpose — a fresh session can check it rather than trust it.
proportion._armCloses: shoulder 1.32 + upper 1.32 = elbow 2.64; + fore 1.18 = wrist 3.82, which is 0.05 HU below the hip. Arms hang correctly at rest with no per-pose correction.
proportion._whySeven: SEVEN, not the old kit's 6.8. 'is he a midget or sum' was a proportion complaint, so the number that drew it gets changed deliberately rather than kept. Seven heads reads adult and composed at 9:16; six-and-a-half reads juvenile. It is one number and it is now wrong once if at all.

contourWeight._note: ONE weight, every part, every pose, both hours. No pressure, no taper, no second pass. The figure's contour is what makes him read against any wall; the room carries NO contour at all and separates by value difference between adjacent flat shapes, which forces the palette to be good.

_quietFloor: BOTH quiet VALUES MOVED at rebuild-03, caught by audit rule 5 on its first run against real plates. night.quiet #6E7C90 measured 3.97:1 against night.ink.ground and dusk.quiet #7A6A58 measured 4.29:1 against dusk.ink.ground — rule 5's floor is 4.5:1 and both captions were under it. Now #8592A6 (5.35:1) and #685A48 (5.49:1). The pair had never been measured because a caption colour looks fine next to a title colour; it is only wrong against the ground it actually sits on, which is what rule 5 samples and prose does not.

plateInk._spec: rebuild-41. The data plates’ inks, ONE SET PER GROUND. Same nine names and meanings as `ink` (ground, band, rule, axis, quiet, structure, subject, subject2, attention) plus three new series inks (subject3 teal, subject4 yellow, subject5 green). `ink` above is unchanged and still serves room/ and overlays/. Which set a plate uses is published on the plate (`ground` in its manifest and slot table); the family table is plateStyle.grounds. The 3D room is the night room at both hours, so dusk carries the same values as night. rebuild-41 (bot answer R41.3): `down` is a fall on every ground; subject2 is the second series only. Violet, a hue the six series and attention do not use, so a fall never reads as the highlight.

hoursAreNotStyles: Two hours of ONE set. Every room exists at both with byte-identical slot boxes, floorLineY and hostAnchor — only the colour table differs. roomHours.episodes picks one per episode and never mixes them inside a video.

typeScale._unit: canvas units at 1920x1080; delivered is x2.
typeScale._floor: 24 units is the hard floor and nothing in the kit is set below it.
typeScale._note: Unchanged from delta-15 — the type scale was never the problem and budget.js's hmtx-derived maxChars is computed against it. Changing it would re-derive 3,033 slot budgets for no reason.

motion._hostNote: AUTHORED micro-offsets, not noise. Identical every loop. The head rotation is degrees about the neck join; shoulderY is canvas units at 1920x1080.
motion._dataNote: A data plate's FRAME breathes and its figures do not. Only the frame's rule lines take the 1px offset. Axes, series, cells and anything a viewer reads a value off stay pinned across all three frames.

plateStyle._spec: rebuild-41 restyle. Everything numeric about how a data plate is drawn, read by engine/grounds.js (the kit) and published for the bot. Canvas units at the plate’s own canvas (1920x1080 or 1080x1920).

grounds._unchanged: overlays/ (source tag, lower third, row band, wipes) keep their look and their `ink`; host/ and room/ are untouched.
grounds._screenKeys: empty since shorts/short-chart moved to charts/short-chart-9x16 (rebuild-41, bot answer R41.4).

plateStyle._seriesOrder: Six series inks in the order a multi-series plate takes them. attention is the sixth and is ALSO the plate’s one accent: a plate that spends attention on the number that matters draws at most five series.

contour._note: ONE weight, every filled shape on a paper plate (furniture and data), both aspects, the room’s outline ink. Screen plates carry none on the data.

plateStyle._barToGap: every bar, pair, step and segment is at least this many times as wide as the gap beside it.
plateStyle._contentFill: the content block (union of the plate’s text and region slots) covers at least this share of the safe area in width AND height. 16:9 safe area is the 5% margin; 9:16 is shorts.readable inside a 5% side margin.
plateStyle._leadFigureSpan: figures/ and shorts/ number plates: the lead figure (the slot(s) set in the plate’s largest role) spans at least this share of the frame width, set to the box width (fit: width).

shorts._note: 9:16 only. Everything a viewer reads sits between y 170 and 1480 of the 1080x1920 frame (YouTube’s buttons and title cover the rest). No type below label (34); headline roles at least statement (64).

cvd.metric: OKLab ΔE between every pair of the six series inks, normal vision and Machado-2009 protan/deutan/tritan at severity 1

contrast._note: Rule 32. Type: every role colour against its plate ground. Non-text: every series ink drawn bare (lines, dots) against the ground; on paper the fill-only inks are exempt because they never appear without the contour, which is 17:1.

downApart._note: OKLab ΔE between down and attention, normal and simulated protan/deutan/tritan. Rule 32.

plateStyle._maxAnisotropy: the safe-area fit may scale one way up to 2x the other, for a layout that is thin in one dimension (a definition card, a big number with one caption). Type scales by the smaller; boxes by their own axis.
